title: Desvignes again, the Four Tones and William Houston
summary: Rejoining Desvignes 1941-47, forming the Four Tones, and the band's becoming Houston's Orchestra.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You string your banjo and guitar opposite then too.

Yes. And I started on the bass violin and played that and I continued on playing the bass violin. And I joined Sidney Desvines band again in 1941 and played with him until 47. And that band broke up. Then the Four Tones came in. That was Fred Minor, he was playing guitar in Sidney Desvines band. Louis Barberand was playing drums. And Alvin Alcorn playing trumpet. So we organized a group and called them the Four Tones. We played for two, three years together. And the remaining part of the band was taken over by Joseph Phillips, trumpet player. That group was called Joseph Phillips' Orchestra. And after about two years, William Houston, the pianist in Sidney Desvines band, bought out the ownership from Joe Phillips. And that's William Houston's Orchestra now.
That's after Sidney Desvines already gave up in...
He left and went to California.
Yes. And we interviewed him out there too. He died, you know, last year.
I'd never met him. Oh, I'd heard the band years ago here. You might have been with them. About 1942, I guess.
I was playing with him then, playing bass violin. We were playing out the Gypsy Tea Room quite a bit then.
And I heard about, I think, at the San Jacinto Club there.
San Jacinto Club also, yes. We played there quite a bit.
In those days, I didn't know everybody in the band. I didn't know for sure who I heard.
